source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels.
source.paleography_note: The layered-witness convention reflects the manuscript-attestation reality: Aramaic DSS fragments are FRAGMENTARY (preserve only portions of chs 1-36); Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus preserves chs 1-32 substantially complete; Ge'ez is the only complete witness but the most distant in time and language from the Aramaic original. Per-verse selection prioritizes the oldest preserved witness; alternate witnesses documented where they differ materially or provide cross-collation value.

verses.text: ונסבו להון נשין כל חד וחד מנהון אתבחר לה אנתה ושריו למעלה עליהן ולסאבה עמהן ואלפו אנון חרשין ולחרסה ולקטיעת שרשין ועקרין ואחויו להון עשבין
verses.translit: wa-něsabū lěhōn něšīn kol ḥad wĕ-ḥad minhōn ʾitběḥar leh ʾinttāh wĕ-šārīw lě-meʿlāh ʿălēhēn wĕ-lě-saʾāḇāh ʿimhēn wa-ʾallēpū ʾinnōn ḥăršīn wĕ-lě-ḥāršāh wĕ-lě-qěṭīʿat šoršīn wĕ-ʿiqqārīn wĕ-ʾaḥwīw lěhōn ʿiśbīn
verses.text_greek: καὶ ἔλαβον ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας ἕκαστος αὐτῶν, ἐξελέξαντο ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας, καὶ ἤρξαντο εἰσπορεύεσθαι πρὸς αὐτάς, καὶ μιαίνεσθαι ἐν αὐταῖς, καὶ ἐδίδαξαν αὐτὰς φαρμακείας καὶ ἐπαοιδὰς καὶ ῥιζοτομίας, καὶ τὰς βοτάνας ἐδήλωσαν αὐταῖς.
verses.text_geez: ወነሥኡ፡ ሎሙ፡ አንስተ፡ ኵሉ፡ አሐዱ፡ አሐዱ፡ ለርእሱ፡ ኀረዩ፡ ለሊሆሙ፡ አንስቲያሆሙ፡ ወአኀዙ፡ ይባኡ፡ ኀቤሆን፡ ወይትጋበሩ፡ ምስሌሆን፡ ወመሀርዎን፡ ሥራዬ፡ ወመሰብርተ፡ ሥሮታት፡ ወአዕሣበ፡ አርአይዎን፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iii 13-18 + 4Q202 1 ii 19-26 (Milik 1976 pp. 150-157) — Aramaic preserves the knowledge-transmission catalog
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CROSS-CORPUS SITE.** The Watchers take human wives, defile themselves with them, and **teach them sorceries (חרשין / φαρμακείας), enchantments (ἐπαοιδάς), root-cutting (κοπή ῥιζῶν / ῥιζοτομίας — pharmacological herbalism), and showed them plants (botany).** This is the FIRST knowledge-transmission instance — wives learn pharmacological/magical arts. Cross-corpus: Gen 6:2; CD 2:17-19; Jub 5:1-2. The 'roots and herbs' theme is paralleled in the apkallū tradition (Mesopotamian sages teaching herbalism/medicine to humans). LENS-RISK: the canon engages this as 'Elohim teach humanity technical arts' — the textual presentation here is morally ambiguous (knowledge as defilement) but later traditions (canon-internal) re-frame as positive technology-transfer. Editor to handle.

verses.text: ואלין הריון מנהון וילדו גברי רברבין רומהון תלת מאה אמין
verses.translit: wĕ-ʾillēn hărīyōn minhōn wĕ-yělidū gibbārīn rabrěbīn rūmhōn tělāt měʾāh ʾammīn
verses.text_greek: αἱ δὲ ἐν γαστρὶ λαβοῦσαι ἐτέκοσαν γίγαντας μεγάλους ἐκ πηχῶν τρισχιλίων.
verses.text_geez: ወፀንሳ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ወወለዳ፡ ሬማ፡ ዐበይተ፡ ዘሠለስቱ፡ ምእት፡ እመት፡ ቆሞሙ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iii 19-21 + 4Q204 1 ii 19-21 (Milik 1976 pp. 152, 178) — Aramaic preserves גברי רברבין 'great mighty ones' (gibborin)
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE — THE GIANTS (Nephilim/Gibborim).** The Watcher-human union produces gibborim (גברי רברבין 'great mighty ones'; Greek γίγαντας 'giants'; Ge'ez ሬማ). **Height notice**: Aramaic 4Q201 reads תלת מאה אמין '300 cubits' (the original; Milik 1976 p. 157); the Greek Akhmim reads τρισχιλίων 'three thousand' (transmission inflation — Greek scribes amplified the giants' height tenfold); Ge'ez follows the Greek with 300 cubits in some mss, 3000 in others. Charles 1912 emends to 3000 following the Greek; Nickelsburg 2001 follows Aramaic 300 (more plausible in context). Cross-corpus: Gen 6:4 (Nephilim, gibborim, men of renown); Num 13:33 (Nephilim spies' report); cf. the giants tradition in 4Q530 (Book of Giants from Qumran). LENS-RISK: the giants-as-literal-physical-giants reading is the popular-fringe canon-engagement site (3000-cubit giants); acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applies. Some patristic readings interpret gibborim figuratively as 'mighty in evil' rather than physical giants — Nickelsburg notes both readings.

verses.text_greek: οὗτοι κατήσθιον τοὺς κόπους τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὡς δὲ οὐχ ὑπέφερον αὐτοὺς τρέφειν οἱ ἄνθρωποι,
verses.translit: houtoi katēsthion tous kopous tōn anthrōpōn, hōs de ouch hypepheron autous trephein hoi anthrōpoi,
verses.text_aramaic: אלין הוו אכלין יגיע אנשא ולא יכלין אנשא לסבלא להון
verses.text_geez: እሉ፡ ይበልዑ፡ ጻማ፡ ሰብእ፡ ወአበዩ፡ ሰብእ፡ አሰሥዮቶሙ፡
verses.notes: The giants devour humanity's produce/labor; humans cannot sustain feeding them.

verses.text_greek: ἐπεστράφησαν οἱ γίγαντες κατὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὥστε κατεσθίειν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: epestraphēsan hoi gigantes kata tōn anthrōpōn, hōste katesthiein autous.
verses.text_geez: ወተመይጠ፡ ሬማ፡ ላዕለ፡ ሰብእ፡ ከመ፡ ይብልዕዎሙ፡
verses.notes: The giants turn cannibal — devouring humanity. The Greek κατεσθίειν 'eat down/devour' is the cannibalism marker.

verses.text_greek: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἁμαρτάνειν ἐν τοῖς πετεινοῖς καὶ τοῖς θηρίοις καὶ τοῖς ἑρπετοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἰχθύσιν, καὶ ἀλλήλων τὰς σάρκας κατεσθίειν, καὶ τὸ αἷμα ἔπινον.
verses.translit: kai ērxanto hamartanein en tois peteinois kai tois thēriois kai tois herpetois kai tois ichthysin, kai allēlōn tas sarkas katesthiein, kai to haima epinon.
verses.text_geez: ወአኀዙ፡ ይኄጥኡ፡ በዖፍ፡ ወበአራዊት፡ ወበዘይትሐወስ፡ ወበዓሣት፡ ወሥጋ፡ በበይናቲሆሙ፡ ይብልዑ፡ ወደመ፡ ይሰትዩ፡
verses.notes: The pre-Noachic dietary indictment: eating birds, beasts, reptiles, fish, and (climactically) human flesh + drinking blood. Cross-corpus: this is the etiology Jewish tradition uses for the Noachic prohibitions (Gen 9:4-5; b. Sanh. 56b). The blood-drinking is THE marker that triggers divine intervention.

verses.text_greek: τότε ἡ γῆ ἐνέτυχεν κατὰ τῶν ἀνόμων.
verses.translit: tote hē gē enetychen kata tōn anomōn.
verses.text_geez: ይእተ፡ አሚረ፡ ምድር፡ ሰከየት፡ ላዕለ፡ ዐማፅያን፡
verses.notes: **The earth's complaint** — sets up the four-archangels intervention in ch 9. The verb enetychen / קבלת 'made appeal / complained' uses the technical-Aramaic legal-petition vocabulary. Cross-corpus: cf. Gen 4:10 (Abel's blood crying from the ground); cf. Rom 8:22 (creation groaning).
